item.title: Ebola response faces setback as transit centre burns down in DR Congo camp
item.description: The enormous challenge of halting the spread of Ebola in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) just became even harder after a key transit centre for patients requiring treatment burned down in Ituri province.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Somali families face renewed violence amid worsening hunger crisis
item.description: Children have been killed and injured in fresh fighting in Baidoa, in Somalia’s South West State, where families were already facing severe hunger and other overlapping crises.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Security Council LIVE: DRC peace deals fail to halt fighting as Ebola deepens crisis
item.description: The Security Council met in New York on the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) Tuesday, where clashes between Government forces and M23 rebels continue in the east, despite a series of peace agreements. Ambassadors focused on ceasefire monitoring, rising tensions between the DRC and Rwanda and the country’s worst Ebola outbreak on record, which has killed more than 3,900 people.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: DRC: Early access to care and oxygen decisive for Ebola patients’ survival – WHO
item.description: In the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), health workers fighting the country’s largest-ever Ebola outbreak are struggling to overcome critical challenges to patient care, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) warned on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Ballot must replace the bullets’, South Sudan tells General Assembly ahead of elections
item.description: South Sudan remains committed to holding general elections in December to conclude its transition period, the country’s Permanent Representative to the United Nations Cecilia Adout Majok Adeng, told the General Assembly on Monday, calling for all sanctions, including the arms embargo to be lifted.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Sudan tells UN: No imposed solutions to country’s conflict
item.description: Sudan’s Foreign Minister addressed the UN General Assembly on Monday in place of Chairperson of the Transitional Sovereignty Council, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, whose visa application was rejected by Washington.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: DR Congo Ebola emergency: Calls grow for urgent humanitarian access
item.description: Aid teams trying to keep deadly Ebola disease from spreading in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) are increasingly concerned about ongoing fighting and violence that has forced thousands of people to flee a displacement camp in the vast, resource-rich east of the country.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN voices grave concern as fighting spreads across northern Ethiopia
item.description: The UN said on Friday it remains gravely concerned by the continued deterioration of the security situation across northern Ethiopia, as fighting spreads across multiple fronts and increasingly disrupts humanitarian operations.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Africa needs its own AI solutions, not borrowed ones, says expert
item.description: Africa should focus its use of technology on solving its own real challenges rather than copying the systems and priorities of other parts of the world.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Sudan’s farmers are ready to return – private investment could get them there
item.description: The war in Sudan has devastated the economy and agricultural production, but a UN-backed plan aims to mobilise private sector investment to help farmers return to their fields.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Peace remains only a promise’ for millions in eastern DR Congo, General Assembly hears
item.description: The Prime Minister of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) cautioned against growing global demand for “blood-stained minerals” in the rush to net-zero, in her speech to the UN General Assembly.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: The Takeaway: UN General Assembly debate Day 1
item.description: War, inequality, climate change and artificial intelligence set the backdrop as world leaders took the floor for the opening day of the UN General Assembly’s annual high-level debate. Against a sombre picture of widening geopolitical divisions and mounting pressure on international law, speakers returned again and again to one central question: can multilateral cooperation deliver when it is needed most? This edition of The Takeaway distils the key points from Day 1.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: DR Congo Ebola outbreak toll exceeds 3,700 deaths
item.description: More than 130 days into the latest Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), health experts said on Wednesday that response efforts have been scaled up significantly and “the first encouraging signs of progress” are now being seen.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: In Tanzania, the sea is moving inland – and taking livelihoods with it
item.description: Along the coast of Tanzania, in East Africa, the Indian Ocean is pushing saltwater ever farther inland, shrinking coconut harvests, driving fish away and leaving some residents wondering how much longer they can stay.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Ebola vaccine research programme begins in DR Congo
item.description: An Ebola vaccine programme is underway in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), involving frontline health workers and others involved in the response.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Women and girls pay high price in DR Congo Ebola outbreak
item.description: The deadly Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has taken a disproportionate toll on women and girls, many of whom are on the frontlines caring for patients as well as their own families despite the high risk of infection.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Ebola responders grapple with widening outbreak in DR Congo
item.description: The deadly Ebola virus outbreak in DR Congo continues to spread across the vast country despite some success in containing it, aid officials said on Tuesday, in a renewed call for international support to help responders on the ground.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘Super El Niño’ deepens hunger crisis in South Sudan – WFP
item.description: The already dire hunger crisis in South Sudan is becoming increasingly critical as violence, extreme weather and dwindling aid leave millions without enough food, the UN World Food Programme (WFP) warned on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN agencies warn humanitarian system in Sudan ‘could collapse’
item.description: UN aid agencies on Monday said they may be forced to scale back humanitarian aid in Sudan – home of the world’s worst hunger and displacement crisis – due to funding shortfalls.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: South Sudan: UNICEF reaches communities cut off by conflict in Jonglei state
item.description: The UN Children’s Fund (UNICEF) and partners have delivered lifesaving assistance to families in conflict-affected communities in South Sudan’s Jonglei state, many of whom had gone months without humanitarian support.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Human cost of violence in South Sudan ‘continues to grow’
item.description: Independent human rights investigators voiced deep concern over growing risks to both civilians and South Sudan’s political transition following their latest fact-finding mission to the world’s youngest nation – their 14th in a decade.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: UN hails Libya election deal as Security Council urges Libyans to seize the moment
item.description: The UN Security Council has welcomed a breakthrough agreement between Libya's rival political blocs, calling it "an important step" towards the country's first national elections in over a decade – while pressing all sides to move quickly from paper to practice.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Ebola response in eastern DR Congo must include food assistance, WFP says
item.description: As Ebola sweeps across the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC), ensuring families meet their basic food needs is crucial to halt the spread of the deadly disease.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Human rights chief Türk renews call for end to spiralling Sudan war
item.description: The ongoing war in Sudan took centre stage at the UN Human Rights Council on Monday where the UN High Commissioner for Human Rights, Volker Türk, led calls for an end to attacks on civilians in “markets, hospitals [and] fuel stations”.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: New reservoir offers innovative solution to South Sudan cattle beef
item.description: At the end of a history-laden path winding through palm trees and scattered ruins – remnants of once-vibrant villages destroyed by cattle raids – lies a rare sight in this dry part of Terekeka county in South Sudan: a sparkling, fresh water source.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Outside forces fuel Sudan war, new report finds
item.description: Foreign recruitment and external support networks are fuelling the brutal conflict in Sudan, independent UN human rights investigators said on Thursday in a new report, calling for accountability as fighting continues between the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) and the paramilitary Rapid Support Forces (RSF).
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Repression of political opposition surges in post-election Zambia
item.description: Following Zambia’s contested presidential and parliamentary elections almost three weeks ago, the crackdown on political opposition has intensified, raising concerns about the future of democracy in the country, according to a UN Human Rights Council-appointed expert.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Sudan: Air attack destroys food aid for families in South Kordofan
item.description: Two truckloads of food aid destined for hungry families in South Kordofan state, Sudan, were destroyed in an aerial attack over the weekend, the World Food Progamme (WFP) said on Wednesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: Response must outpace spread of Ebola: UN relief chief
item.description: The world must move faster to contain an Ebola outbreak in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) that is growing exponentially, the UN’s Emergency Relief Coordinator warned on Tuesday.
item.source: UN News - Global perspective Human stories

item.title: ‘The lake is our life’: Protecting a shared lifeline in Uganda
item.description: On the shores of Nkondo, in Uganda’s Kikuube district, the day begins before sunrise. Fishers enter the lake to fish, while families around Lake Albert rely on its waters for food, income and daily survival.
